name: Shared identity Astro session API compatibility correction
phase: Specification only; implementation requires separate explicit authorization
objective: Make the shared identity session adapter compatible with asynchronous Astro session reads and synchronous destruction without changing authorization, validation, expiry or cleanup semantics.
implementationScope: Modify only these four existing files; add no implementation files or FOOD-specific logic.

discoveryEvidence.observedContract: Installed Astro get is asynchronous; set, delete and destroy are synchronous; regenerate is asynchronous.
discoveryEvidence.rootCause: AstroPrincipalSessionStore.getSession currently validates the immediate session.get return without awaiting it, so an actual Astro Promise can be mistaken for malformed session data. Existing synchronous fakes conceal the incompatibility.

astroSessionLikeContract.set: Remain synchronous with existing arguments and void return.
astroSessionLikeContract.delete: Remain synchronous with existing key argument and void return.
astroSessionLikeContract.destroy: Support void | Promise<void>; existing callers may continue to await destruction.

adapterRequirements: Await session.get(AUTHENTICATED_PRINCIPAL_SESSION_KEY) before absence checks or payload validation.
Keep awaited session acquisition outside the malformed-payload validation catch. A rejected asynchronous get is a storage/session-access failure, not a malformed payload.
Propagate read failures to DefaultSessionPrincipalResolver's existing unavailable path; do not delete session data or reach principal lookup after a rejected read.
Preserve existing synchronous set/delete behavior and existing awaiting of regenerate/destroy.
Keep PrincipalSessionStore's existing asynchronous public operations unchanged. DefaultSessionPrincipalResolver already awaits store reads/destruction and needs no implementation change.
Construction remains synchronous and I/O-free: no session read, session mutation, clock invocation or database access during construction.
preservedSemantics: Missing resolved session data returns null without cleanup.
Malformed resolved session data deletes only the principal-session key through existing malformed-session cleanup.
Expired session data deletes the principal-session key; preserve the existing expiry boundary.
Malformed/expired cleanup exceptions fail closed and propagate to the resolver's existing unavailable path.
Missing, inactive or mismatched principals retain existing resolver destruction behavior, including unavailable on destruction failure.
Canonical principal and session validation, authenticated-principal session key, payload version, TTL and expiry rules remain unchanged.
Preserve fresh principal resolution and fail-closed authorization; do not introduce principal lookup on missing, malformed, expired or unreadable sessions.
Synchronous and asynchronous destruction are both supported; awaiting synchronous Astro destruction does not prove durable storage cleanup. Framework persistence remains outside this correction.
tests: Add or adjust tests using a genuinely Astro-like fake with asynchronous get, synchronous set/delete/destroy and asynchronous regenerate.
A delayed valid asynchronous read is awaited, returns the validated session and never deletes it.
Missing asynchronous reads preserve null/unauthenticated behavior without cleanup or principal lookup.
Malformed asynchronous results trigger existing principal-key deletion and no principal lookup.
Expired asynchronous results trigger existing principal-key deletion; test the unchanged exact expiry boundary.
Rejected asynchronous get maps to resolver unavailable with zero deletion, zero destruction and zero principal lookup.
Malformed/expired deletion exceptions fail closed through resolver unavailable without principal lookup.
A valid asynchronously read session passes its exact canonical principal ID to principal lookup.
Missing/inactive/mismatched principals retain existing destruction behavior, including failure handling.
Synchronous destroy works, existing asynchronous destroy remains supported and existing synchronous read fakes remain valid regressions.
Construction performs zero session or database operations and does not invoke the clock.
Session creation preserves regeneration ordering, synchronous set arguments, key, validated payload and TTL.
requiredValidation: Run affected identity runtime regressions, including principal login/logout runtime tests.
Run affected Sesh runtime regressions without modifying Sesh source.
Run strict TypeScript checks for the modified identity/session files.
Run the normal build; do not fix unrelated baseline failures within this correction.
excludedScope: No FOOD-specific logic or FOOD source changes.
No production route/UI changes or Sesh source changes.
No changes to River OS authentication/access-key semantics.
No D1 schemas, migrations, database configuration or provisioning.
No deployment, migration execution, production access or production data changes.
No authorization redesign or unrelated subsystem changes.
currentTaskBoundary: Create only this specification. Do not implement, modify existing files, stage, commit, deploy, migrate or touch production data.
nextStep: Review this specification before separately authorizing the four-file shared identity compatibility correction; FOOD-001G remains deferred until compatibility correction and regressions pass.
